title: News Gapper
teaches: The News Gapper as we trade it: a fresh named catalyst, most often an earnings report, gaps a liquid stock up on at least three times its average volume; the gap holds and the day closes green in the upper half; the buy is the first pullback and reclaim, a market order as price trades over the prior day's high after two down days or an inside day that hold the gap-day low, or day one over the opening-range high for an A+; the stop sits a few cents under the pullback low, the first sell is a judgment, usually day 3 or later into a 3, 5 or 7 day push, with the rest on the 9 or 20 EMA trail, and a loss taken at the stop is the system working.

walkthroughs.title: ULTA, March 2016: a big gap and a shallow pullback
steps: ULTA reported March 10, 2016. Next day it gapped up 14.2% on 4.8 times normal volume and closed near the high.
A big gap out of a correction. Then four quiet days, only 2.8% deep, and it never lost the gap-day low.
After an inside day, day 6 takes out its high: buy at market, 190.69. Stop just under the pullback low, 186.55.
A close under the gap-day low says we're wrong. Never happened. It ran to 12.1R: sell into a push, trail the rest.

walkthroughs.title: TWLO, February 2018: a gap through the 200-day
steps: TWLO spent 3 months bottoming. Then its February 13, 2018 report gapped it 10.0% the next day, on 8.3 times volume.
That gap goes straight through the 200-day. Then a 6-session pullback that holds the gap-day low. The 50-day's still under the 200.
After an inside day, day 8 trades over its high. Buy at market, 33.55. Stop 32.59, under the inside day's low.
Close under the gap-day low and it's wrong. Instead, 3R in 4 sessions, and 24.1R at its best.

walkthroughs.title: NFLX, October 2024: new highs from a tight base
steps: October 18, 2024, the day after its report, NFLX gaps 7.3% to new highs on 5.6 times volume. Closes near the top.
It came out of a tight base. Then a 4-session pullback, only 2.9% deep, holding the gap-day low.
After an inside-day hammer, day 6 takes out its high. Buy at market, 75.62. Stop under the pullback low, 74.38.
A red first day or a filled gap would've said no. Instead, a two-month run. Sell into a push, trail the rest.

questions.q: A stock gaps up on its earnings report. It never trades back to yesterday's close and ends green near the high. What is it?
choices: A News Gapper, the gap held
A failed gap, it'll fill later
A Kicker, a positioning gap
Nothing yet, wait for the fill
questions.answer: A News Gapper, the gap held
questions.why: That's a News Gapper. Named news, here the report, and a gap that holds. Holding means two things. Price never trades back to yesterday's close, and the day closes green in the upper half of its range. That tells you the buyers who showed up on the news stayed all day. A red close or a filled gap is a different story, and not one we buy.
questions.lesson_line: Named news, a gap that holds, a green close up high. That's the News Gapper.

wrong.A failed gap, it'll fill later: Nothing filled. It never got back to yesterday's close, so there's no failure to call.
wrong.A Kicker, a positioning gap: A Kicker comes after a weak red close and rarely has a headline. This one gapped on its report.
wrong.Nothing yet, wait for the fill: We never want the fill. A gap that fills has failed, and this one held.

questions.simple: A News Gapper. Real news plus a gap that holds all day means the buyers stuck around.

reasons: both cited facts come from one criteria card, not a second source
the upper-half line is a proposed card criterion

questions.q: A stock gaps 9% this morning and you can't find any news behind it. You don't treat it as a News Gapper.
questions.why: True. No named news, no News Gapper. The news is the reason buyers keep coming after day one. A beat with a raise, or a deal that changes the business, gives big buyers something to act on for weeks. A gap on nothing has nothing behind it once the open is over. Before I touch any gapper, I want to say in one line why it gapped.
questions.lesson_line: If you can't name the news, it isn't a News Gapper.
questions.simple: True. Without news you can name, buyers have no reason to keep coming after the open.

reasons: tied to held decision D-032 (catalyst types)

deeper.counter: Bonde puts media mentions and analyst upgrades in the low-probability bucket: they rarely follow through. Earnings, new products and raised guidance are what start the long runs.

questions.q: Did this gap hold?
choices: Yes, no fill and a close up high
No, it traded back to the prior close
Yes, any open over the close holds
Can't tell until tomorrow's close
questions.answer: Yes, no fill and a close up high
questions.why: It held. The low of the day sits above the prior day's high, so price never came near yesterday's close. Then CCJ closed at 98% of its range, right at the top. Everybody who paid up on the news was still happy at the bell. Nobody was dumping it into the close. That's what I want to see before I even think about the pullback. A gap that fills tells you sellers took it all back.
questions.lesson_line: A held gap never sees the prior close, and the day closes strong.

wrong.No, it traded back to the prior close: Look at the low. It stayed above the prior day's high, so it never came back to the close.
wrong.Yes, any open over the close holds: An open proves nothing. Plenty of gaps open up and fill by lunch. Holding means no fill and a strong close.
wrong.Can't tell until tomorrow's close: The gap day tells you on its own. Judge the fill and the close tonight, then plan the pullback.

questions.simple: Yes. Price never got back to yesterday's close and it finished near the high, so the buyers held it.

deeper.counter: A gap can stay open and still be weak. NFLX, 2018: a 9.2% gap on 3.3x volume. The low of 35.65 stayed above the prior close of 34.64, so the gap never filled. But the day closed at 35% of its range, short of the upper-half test. Not filling is one test. The close is another.

reasons: both cited facts come from one criteria card
the card says upper half for the key and also calls a lower-half close a B-, so the key follows the stricter line

questions.story: May 2025. The last bar is the gap day, a 6.2% gap on news.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: On the pullback buy, the stop goes a few cents under the pullback ___.
questions.why: Low. On the pullback buy the stop goes a few cents under the pullback low.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: a few cents under the pullback low.

questions.q: A stock's up 11% pre-market on a big beat. Bonde made his best EP money buying there, so we buy pre-market too.
questions.why: False. We don't buy before the bell, and we don't buy after hours either. Bonde did make his big EP money pre-market, and I get why. But pre-market there's no real range yet, so there's no low to put your stop under. Wait for the open. Let the first 5 or 30 minutes set a high and a low. Then buy as it trades over that high, with the stop under the low.
questions.lesson_line: No pre-market buys. Let the open set the range, then buy the trigger.
questions.simple: False. Before the open there's no range to stop against, so we wait for regular hours and buy the trigger.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (E58, no buys outside regular hours)

deeper.counter: Kullamägi rarely trades extended hours either. He prefers to wait for the opening-range highs.

questions.q: Our market filter runs Green, Yellow, Orange, Red. In which readings do you take new news gapper buys?
choices: Green or Yellow, sized to it
Orange or Red, fear drives gaps
Green only, never Yellow
Any of them, a good headline wins
questions.answer: Green or Yellow, sized to it
questions.why: Green or Yellow, and the color sets how much. Green is full risk for the grade. Yellow is smaller and fewer. The reason is simple. Breakouts and gaps fail more when the market isn't behind them, so as the color weakens we put less on. A string of failed buys then costs you a little instead of a lot. Orange is only for an A+, our very cleanest setup. In Red, I'm mostly in cash.
questions.lesson_line: Check the market color first. Green or Yellow for gappers, sized to it.

wrong.Green only, never Yellow: Yellow's fine. You just go smaller and take fewer.
wrong.Orange or Red, fear drives gaps: Orange is for an A+ only, and Red is mostly cash. That's where you pull back, not press.
wrong.Any of them, a good headline wins: A great headline doesn't switch the market off. The color still sets how much you trade.

questions.simple: Green or Yellow. As the color weakens we risk less, so a run of failed buys costs less.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (F65 market reading)

questions.q: Most of the earnings gappers you'll trade show up in a 3 to 4 week stretch each quarter.
questions.why: True. Most companies report in the same few weeks every quarter, so that's when the gaps pile up. That's when I'm scanning hardest every night. Have your scans and your list ready before the season starts, not halfway through it. Then go through the new gappers one by one each night and mark your levels.
questions.lesson_line: Earnings season is gapper season. Be ready before it starts.
questions.simple: True. Most companies report in the same few weeks, so that's when the gaps bunch up.

reasons: one cited fact only (our card)
a timing claim about the calendar that can change

questions.q: How much volume does a News Gapper need by the close?
choices: At least 3 times the 50-day average
Any volume if the gap is big
Just above the 50-day average
Less than the 50-day average
questions.why: At least 3 times the 50-day average, and on pace for it by the opening-range buy. Kullamagi: volume is the number one thing to focus on.
questions.lesson_line: Three times average volume is the line.

wrong.Any volume if the gap is big: A big gap on thin volume is the trap; volume is the line.
wrong.Just above the 50-day average: Just above average is the B- zone, below the line.
wrong.Less than the 50-day average: Below average volume is the opposite of a news gap.

questions.q: The pullback buy waits for two down days or an inside day whose closes all hold the gap-day low.
questions.why: True. After two down days or an inside day that keep every close above the gap-day low, the buy is a market order over the prior day's high.
questions.lesson_line: The pullback must hold the gap-day low on every close.

questions.q: In the first ten sessions, which event ends the setup?
choices: A close under the gap-day low
An inside day
Two down days that hold the low
A quiet day on lighter volume
questions.answer: A close under the gap-day low
questions.why: A close under the gap-day low. The gap fills or the stock closes under the gap-day low in the first ten sessions.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the gap-day low ends it.

wrong.An inside day: An inside day is a pullback pattern we want.
wrong.Two down days that hold the low: Two down days that hold the gap-day low are the pullback itself.
wrong.A quiet day on lighter volume: A quiet day on lighter volume is part of a healthy pullback.

questions.q: A gap on good news that closes red is a News Failure, not a News Gapper.
questions.why: True. A red close after good news is the News Failure. Same headline, opposite trade.
questions.lesson_line: Same headline, red close: a different trade.

questions.q: Four stocks gap up this morning on four different headlines. Which one has the news that can carry it for weeks?
choices: A beat with a raised outlook
A mention on a morning TV show
One analyst upgrade to a buy
A vague press release about plans
questions.answer: A beat with a raised outlook
questions.why: The beat with a raised outlook. That changes what the business will earn, so big buyers have to re-price it. That can take weeks, and that's the run you want. A TV mention or one analyst's upgrade changes nothing about the business. Those pops fade fast. Earnings and really notable news are where I put my attention.
questions.lesson_line: Earnings with a raise is real fuel. A mention or an upgrade isn't.

wrong.A mention on a morning TV show: A TV mention doesn't change the business. Those pops rarely follow through.
wrong.One analyst upgrade to a buy: One opinion, nothing new in the numbers. Upgrades rarely follow through.
wrong.A vague press release about plans: Plans aren't earnings. If you can't say what changed, buyers can't either.

questions.simple: The beat with a raise. It changes what the company will earn, so buyers have a reason to keep coming.

reasons: tied to held decision D-032 (catalyst types)

deeper.counter: Bonde says earnings, new products and raised guidance often start multi-month rallies, while media mentions and upgrades have a low probability of follow-through.

questions.q: When do we skip a news gapper's pullback buy?
choices: A report is due within 3 sessions
The stock is up on the day
Volume is above average
The market is Green
questions.answer: A report is due within 3 sessions
questions.why: A report is due within 3 sessions. We take no new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report.
questions.lesson_line: No new buys in the 3 days before a report.

wrong.The stock is up on the day: Being up on the day is how a reclaim looks.
wrong.Volume is above average: Above-average volume is a plus for a gapper.
wrong.The market is Green: Green is the reading we want.

questions.q: A stock gaps on a big beat and raised guidance. With numbers that good, you judge the numbers first and the chart second.
questions.why: False. The chart comes first. The numbers are known the second they hit the wire. What I need to know is whether buyers are acting on them, and only the chart shows that. I want to see it hold the gap and close up high. Strong sales and earnings still count. They raise the grade, and the grade sets the size. But a great report on a chart that won't hold is a pass.
questions.lesson_line: Good numbers raise the grade. The chart decides.
questions.simple: False. The chart comes first, because it shows whether buyers are actually acting on the numbers.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (D40, the chart comes first)

questions.q: You bought the reclaim, and an hour later volume really kicks in. Adding more shares there is our normal plan.
questions.why: False. We buy the full size at one price with one stop. The stop set your size before you bought. Add later at a higher price with the same stop and you're risking more than you planned. Adding to a working winner on strength does happen, but it's rare and a feel call, never the plan. If you liked it that much, the size should have been there at the trigger.
questions.lesson_line: One buy, one price, one stop. An add is rare, never the plan.
questions.simple: False. An add is rare, and it comes at a higher price with the same stop, so you'd risk more than planned.

reasons: one cited fact only (rulebook A5)
rests on the owner's rulebook

questions.q: Where's 3R on this trade?
questions.why: $110.84. One R is your risk per share, 105.11 minus 103.20. Take three of those and stack them on top of the 105.11 fill, not the stop. You land on 110.84. We count in R because one R is exactly what the stop put on the line. Know where 3R sits before the open. But it's a mark, not a sell order. The first sell is a judgment, and TGT kept going well past it.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. It's a mark, not a sell order.
questions.simple: It's 110.84. Gains are counted in R, so each win is measured against what the stop put at risk.

deeper.example: TGT was bought at 105.11 with the stop at 103.20, a stop 1.8% away. It ran to 12.0R. So 3R at 110.84 was only a mark on the way.

reasons: a computed key
rests on the owner's rulebook (B19 first trim)

wrong.$108.93: That's three R added to the stop. Count from your fill.
wrong.$107.02: That's only one R above the fill. You need three.
wrong.$99.38: Wrong direction. 3R sits above your fill, not below it.

questions.story: August 2019. You bought the first pullback reclaim after its report gap. Fill 105.11, stop 103.20.

questions.q: Gap day: low 100.00, high 110.00, close 107.00. Where in the range did it close, from 0 to 1?
questions.why: 0.70. The close minus the low is 107 minus 100. Divide that by the range, 110 minus 100. That is in the upper half, so this day meets the close test for a held gap. A held gap also needs the day never to trade back to the prior close.
questions.lesson_line: Close minus low, over the range. Upper half passes the close test.
questions.simple: The close is 0.70 of the way up the range. That is the upper half.

reasons: a computed key

wrong.0.30: Measured down from the high, not up from the low.
wrong.0.97: Divided the close by the high and skipped the low.
wrong.0.07: Divided by the low, not by the range.

questions.q: Where does the stop go on the pullback buy?
choices: A few cents under the pullback low
Under the gap-day low, however far
At the prior close, the gap-fill price
1% under the pullback low for room
questions.answer: A few cents under the pullback low
questions.why: A few cents under the pullback low. We set the stop first and size from it. The gap-day low is the line a close must hold, not the stop. There is no porosity: the stop is the exit and it only moves up. On day one the stop goes a few cents under the day's low at the buy.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sits under the pullback low.

wrong.Under the gap-day low, however far: The gap-day low is the line a close must hold. The stop is a few cents under the pullback low.
wrong.At the prior close, the gap-fill price: The prior close is the gap-fill price. The stop goes a few cents under the pullback low, not there.
wrong.1% under the pullback low for room: No porosity: the stop is a few cents under the low, not a 1% cushion.

questions.simple: Put the stop a few cents under the pullback low, because the stop is the exit and gets no cushion.

reasons: the stop rule is the owner's rulebook default (F62)

questions.q: Your gapper's running and you've sold some. You trail the rest on the 20 EMA if it's fast, the 9 EMA if it's steadier.
questions.why: False, it's flipped. A fast mover rides the 9 EMA, so that's the line you trail it on. A steadier one rides the 20 EMA. Trail a fast stock on the 20 and you hand back a big chunk before you're out. Trail a slow one on the 9 and its normal wiggles shake you out early. Sell what's left on a close under the line, not on an intraday dip.
questions.lesson_line: Fast mover, 9 EMA. Steadier one, 20 EMA. Out on a close under it.
questions.simple: False. Fast movers trail on the 9 EMA and steadier ones on the 20 EMA, the line each one rides.

reasons: the trail pairing is the owner's rulebook default (E52), and the question swaps the pair

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: We often sell into a 3, 5 or ___ day push.
questions.why: 7. We often sell into a 3, 5 or 7 day push, or at about 5 to 10R. The first sell is a judgment, not a fixed third at 3R. The rest can trail the 9 EMA or the 20 EMA.
questions.lesson_line: A 3, 5 or 7 day push is often the place for the first sell.
questions.simple: We often sell into a 3, 5 or 7 day push, and the first sell is a judgment call.

reasons: the trim levels are the owner's rulebook defaults (E51) and are marked adjustable

questions.q: Is that a true gap?
choices: Yes, the low is over the prior high
No, it only opened over the close
No, it traded back into the old range
Yes, heavy volume makes it true
questions.answer: Yes, the low is over the prior high
questions.why: Yes. Look at the low of the day. It's above the prior day's high, so the whole day traded above yesterday's range. That leaves a hole on the chart. Nobody got a chance to buy at yesterday's prices. That's a true gap, and it's one of the marks of an A+ gap. AMZN gapped 8.8% here, and the hole stayed open all day.
questions.lesson_line: A true gap leaves a hole. The day's low stays above the prior high.

wrong.No, it only opened over the close: The open doesn't decide it, the low does. This low stayed above the prior high.
wrong.No, it traded back into the old range: It didn't. Every bar of that day sits above the prior high.
wrong.Yes, heavy volume makes it true: Volume's a separate question. A true gap is about where the low sits against the prior high.

questions.simple: Yes. The whole day traded above yesterday's high, so the gap left a hole nobody filled.

reasons: the 10% size is no longer tested (D-033); the true-gap test is ChartSchool's

questions.story: October 2017. The last bar is the gap day, the morning after its report.

questions.q: A true gap means the day's low stays above the prior day's high.
questions.why: True. For an up gap, the low must be higher than the previous day's high.
questions.lesson_line: A true gap leaves a hole above yesterday's high.

questions.q: The 50-day average volume is 4 million shares. The gap day trades 13 million. What is the multiple?
questions.why: 3.25x. Divide gap-day volume by the 50-day average: 13 million over 4 million. That clears the line of at least 3 times. The line is for the close, and the stock must be on pace for it by the buy.
questions.lesson_line: Volume multiple is today over the 50-day average.
questions.simple: Divide 13 million by 4 million to get 3.25, which clears the line of at least 3 times.

reasons: computed key
the 3 times line is a proposed card number

wrong.0.31x: Flipped it: divided the average by the gap-day volume.
wrong.2.25x: Used the extra volume over the average, not the whole day.

questions.q: This morning it trades through 75.58. What's the play?
questions.story: October 2024. A 7.3% earnings gap on 5.6x volume closed at 92% of its range. Four days of pullback, 2.9% deep, held the gap-day low. The last bar is a hammer and an inside day, high 75.58.
choices: Market buy, stop under the pullback low
Pass, day one was the only entry
Wait for the gap to fill, then buy
Limit buy down at the gap-day low
questions.answer: Market buy, stop under the pullback low
questions.why: Buy it at market, right as it goes through 75.58. Look at that last candle first. A hammer, and an inside day too. That's a very good look, and today's the buy day. The gap was strong, 7.3% on 5.6x volume with a close at 92% of the range. The pullback was small and quiet, 2.9% over four days, and it held the gap-day low. Your stop goes a few cents under the pullback low, 74.38, about 1.6% away. Tight, and right where I like it. NFLX went on to a two-month run from there.
questions.lesson_line: Pullback holds, price clears yesterday's high, you buy.

wrong.Wait for the gap to fill, then buy: A gap that fills has failed. That's the last thing you want to see.
wrong.Pass, day one was the only entry: Day one isn't the only way in. The first pullback and reclaim is the main buy.
wrong.Limit buy down at the gap-day low: That waits for weakness under the market. We buy strength, as it clears yesterday's high.

questions.simple: Buy at market as it clears the hammer's high. The pullback held, buyers are back, and the stop is tight.

reasons: tied to held decision D-033 (gap floor; story gap moved to 12%)
fixed before

questions.q: Can you take it?
questions.story: Your gapper pulls back. On day 3 it closes under the gap-day low. On day 4 it rallies and trades over the prior day's high.
choices: No, the setup died on day 3
Yes, the reclaim is the trigger
Yes, at half size to cut risk
Wait, a higher close revives it
questions.answer: No, the setup died on day 3
questions.why: No, it's done. The gap-day low is the line the buyers drew. A close under it means sellers took the gap back. That happened on day 3, before any reclaim, so the setup broke first. A pop on day 4 doesn't undo that. I'd let it go and see if it builds something new later.
questions.lesson_line: Break the gap-day low before the reclaim and there's no buy.

wrong.Yes, the reclaim is the trigger: A reclaim only counts if the pullback held the gap-day low. This one didn't.
wrong.Yes, at half size to cut risk: Half size on a broken setup is still a broken setup.
wrong.Wait, a higher close revives it: Nothing revives it. The close under the gap-day low ended it.

questions.simple: No. A close under the gap-day low means sellers took the gap back, and day 4 can't fix that.

reasons: both cited facts come from one criteria card
the invalidation line is a proposed card criterion

questions.q: Buy it here or pass?
questions.story: Your buy level is 40.00, yesterday's high. You got pulled away from the desk, and now it's 10:30 and the stock's at 41.80.
choices: Pass, that's chasing it
Buy, the reclaim is confirmed
Buy half size to cut the risk
Buy with a wider stop to fit
questions.why: Pass. 41.80 is more than 4% over the 40.00 level, and we don't buy more than 4% past the buy point. Here's what chasing really costs you. Your stop still sits under the buy point, so the distance to it gets bigger. Same dollar risk, fewer shares. And you're buying after the easy part already happened. If a day gaps past your level, a morning flush that curls back up is the other way in. Otherwise, let it go.
questions.lesson_line: Miss it before you chase it. Another one's coming.

wrong.Buy, the reclaim is confirmed: It did confirm. It's also too far gone. Past 4% is a chase.
wrong.Buy half size to cut the risk: Size doesn't fix a chase. The line is 4% at any size.
wrong.Buy with a wider stop to fit: The stop goes where the chart says, not where it fits. A wider stop just hides the chase.

questions.simple: Pass. Your stop stays under the level, so buying this far up means fewer shares for the same risk.

deeper.trap: It is tempting to think a smaller buy or a wider stop repairs a late entry. It does not. Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays under the buy point, so the distance grows and the shares shrink. At 41.80 against a 40.00 reclaim, the answer is to pass.

reasons: the 4% chase line is the owner's rulebook (C28)
the reference level (reclaim or base pivot) is held under D-022

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: A contract headline hits at 7:30 am. The stock is up 11% pre-market on big volume.
choices: Wait for the opening range, then decide
Buy now with a market order
Buy half now, half at the open
Place a stop-limit just under the gap
questions.answer: Wait for the opening range, then decide
questions.why: Wait. We never buy before the open. The opening range forms first, and the day-one buy, if any, comes over its high in regular hours.
questions.lesson_line: No pre-market buys. Let the opening range form.

wrong.Buy now with a market order: Entries are market orders in regular hours, not pre-market.
wrong.Buy half now, half at the open: Half a pre-market buy is still a pre-market buy.
wrong.Place a stop-limit just under the gap: A stop-limit under the gap is not an entry plan.

questions.q: What do you do with it?
questions.story: Your gapper is up 7R after four straight up days. Two of those days gapped up, and each day's range was wider than the last.
choices: Sell a big part into the run
Hold it all, the trail is the exit
Add, momentum's strongest here
Sell everything at tomorrow's open
questions.answer: Sell a big part into the run
questions.why: Sell a big part into it. Four straight up days, two of them gaps, ranges getting wider every day. That's a climax run. It's the move everyone chases, and it's where a stock is most stretched. At 7R you've got a lot to give back if it snaps. So I'm selling a good chunk into that strength. How much is a judgment call. Adding up here is the one thing I won't do.
questions.lesson_line: A climax run on your stock is when you sell a big part into it.

wrong.Hold it all, the trail is the exit: The trail's for what's left. A climax run is when you sell some.
wrong.Add, momentum's strongest here: Never into a climax. The top of a burst is the worst spot to buy more.
wrong.Sell everything at tomorrow's open: A big part is the call, not all of it. Keep some on the trail.

questions.simple: Sell a big part. A climax run is when a stock is most stretched and has the most to give back.

deeper.trap: The trap is thinking the strongest move is the safest to hold or add to. Three to five straight up days with gaps and range expansion is a climax run. Buying the third gap of a parabolic burst is also a listed mistake. Strength here is the reason to sell a big part.

reasons: the climax sale is a judgment call in the owner's rulebook (C34)

questions.q: Do you sell any here?
questions.story: You bought this morning at 50.00 with the stop at 48.00, so 3R is 56.00. By 2:00 the stock's trading 56.00.
choices: Hold, it's only day 1
Sell a third now at 56.00
Sell it all now at 56.00
Sell half and raise the stop
questions.why: Hold it. I very rarely sell on the day I buy, and I wait until day 3 at the earliest most of the time. 3R in a few hours is a great start, not a finish line. Only about three in ten buys ever reach 3R. When you get one that's working this fast, give it room. The first sell is a judgment, often into a 3, 5 or 7 day push.
questions.lesson_line: 3R on day 1 isn't a sell signal. Let it work.

wrong.Sell a third now at 56.00: A fixed third at 3R isn't how we sell. The first sell is a judgment, and day 1 is too early.
wrong.Sell it all now at 56.00: That caps your best kind of trade at 3R. Give a fast starter room.
wrong.Sell half and raise the stop: Half is still a day-1 sell. Wait until day 3 at the earliest.

questions.simple: Hold. Few buys ever reach 3R, so when one works this fast, you give it room to run.

reasons: the open-trim rule is the owner's rulebook (F63)

questions.q: Your gapper's working. Somewhere between 2R and 5R, or at your first sell, you can move the stop up to breakeven.
questions.why: True. Once the stop's at breakeven, the trade can't turn into a loser. That's a great feeling. But move it too early and a normal pullback tags it, and you're out of a good trade for nothing. So it's a judgment, anywhere from 2R to 5R, or when you make your first sell. After that the stop only goes up.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven somewhere from 2R to 5R. After that the stop only goes up.
questions.simple: True. Breakeven takes the loss off the table, but too early a normal pullback stops you out.

reasons: the rulebook gives a range of 2R to 5R, and the first-trim default is the card's

questions.q: Is this a day-one buy for you?
questions.story: A stock gaps 12% on its report. At 9:50 it trades over its 5-minute high, still above the open. It's already done its full average daily volume. The low of the day is 2% under the price.
choices: Yes, market buy, stop under the low
No, day one is never a buy here
Half now, half at the close
Buy tomorrow's open instead
questions.answer: Yes, market buy, stop under the low
questions.why: Yes, buy it at market. That's the A+ way in. It's over the opening-range high, it's holding above the open, and it's already traded a whole day's average volume by 9:50. That's big buyers showing up at once. Your stop goes a few cents under the low of the day, about 2% away. Tight risk on a stock this hot is exactly what I want. I love trading earnings gappers on day one.
questions.lesson_line: Day one over the opening-range high, on hot volume, is a buy.

wrong.No, day one is never a buy here: Day one over the opening-range high, with volume like this, is one we take.
wrong.Half now, half at the close: That's two prices. We buy the full size at one price with one stop.
wrong.Buy tomorrow's open instead: The trigger fired today. Tomorrow's open could be anywhere, with no low to stop against.

questions.simple: Yes. It cleared the opening-range high on huge early volume, and a stop under the low of the day keeps the risk small.

reasons: rests on held decision D-086 (day one against the reclaim)
also D-005 (day-one stop)
fixed before

deeper.example: Kullamägi wants massive volume near the open, ideally the average daily volume in the first 15 to 20 minutes or even quicker.

questions.q: Which lesson owns the day, and which the pullback buy?
questions.story: The gap day is a report's reaction day on an established leader clearing a four-month base.
choices: PEG owns the day; we teach the buy
We own the day and the buy both
Gap Support owns first pullback
Episodic Pivot owns day; no buy
questions.answer: PEG owns the day; we teach the buy
questions.why: The PEG owns the day. The pullback buy is taught here. A report's reaction day on an established leader clearing its base is the PEG. The first-pullback entry on either is taught here. An Episodic Pivot is the first gap in six months on a neglected name.
questions.lesson_line: A report day on a leader is a PEG. The pullback entry is taught here.

wrong.We own the day and the buy both: The PEG lesson owns a report reaction day on a leader.
wrong.Gap Support owns first pullback: Gap Support is the later test of the gap-up low, not the first pullback.
wrong.Episodic Pivot owns day; no buy: An Episodic Pivot is a neglected name, not a leader clearing a base.

questions.simple: The PEG lesson owns the report day on a leader, and this lesson teaches the pullback buy on either kind of gap.

reasons: tied to held decision D-002 (scope of this lesson)
fixed before

questions.q: Gapper or failure?
questions.story: A contract headline gaps a stock up 8% at the open. By the close it's 2% under yesterday's close.
choices: A News Failure, no buy
A News Gapper, great headline
A News Gapper, buy the pullback
A Kicker, the close was weak
questions.why: That's a News Failure. Good news, and it still closed red, under yesterday's close. Think about who's holding it now. Everyone who bought the gap is under water, and a lot of them want out. That supply sits right overhead. Same headline as a gapper, opposite trade. I'm not buying that one, no matter how good the news sounds.
questions.lesson_line: Great news, red close. That's a failure, not a buy.

wrong.A News Gapper, great headline: The headline doesn't decide it, the close does. This one closed red.
wrong.A News Gapper, buy the pullback: There's no gapper to pull back from. The gap didn't hold.
wrong.A Kicker, the close was weak: A Kicker needs the weak red close the day before, then a gap. Here the weak close came after the gap.

questions.simple: A News Failure, no buy. It closed under yesterday's close, so every gap buyer is under water.

deeper.counter: Good news does not decide it. The close does. A gap that holds closes green in the upper half. One that closes under the prior close is a News Failure, even on the same headline. Check the close before you call the headline good.

reasons: both cited facts come from one criteria card
the News Failure trade is not taught here (D-001)

questions.q: Which setup are you looking at?
questions.story: Monday ends with a weak red close. Tuesday opens 2% higher on normal volume, and there's no headline anywhere.
choices: A Kicker, a positioning gap
A News Gapper, the gap is enough
A PEG, it gapped on volume
An Episodic Pivot, a fresh gap
questions.why: A Kicker. A weak red close, then a small gap up the next day with no news. That's positioning, not a headline. It's a real setup, just a different one with its own rules. For a News Gapper I need news I can name. This had none.
questions.lesson_line: Weak red close, small gap, no news. That's a Kicker.

wrong.A News Gapper, the gap is enough: No news, no News Gapper. A gap alone isn't enough.
wrong.A PEG, it gapped on volume: A PEG is a report's reaction day on a leader. There was no report here, and the volume was normal.
wrong.An Episodic Pivot, a fresh gap: An EP re-prices a neglected stock on a big surprise. A small gap with no news isn't that.

questions.simple: A Kicker. A small gap after a weak red close, with no news, is positioning, not a News Gapper.

reasons: the Kicker line comes from one criteria card
the lookalike tells are proposed card criteria

questions.q: Which trade is this?
questions.story: Five weeks after a report gap, the stock dips to the gap-up low, undercuts it a little, and closes back over it.
choices: Gap Support, the later test
A News Gapper pullback buy
A News Failure, the gap broke
A PEG, it's an earnings stock
questions.why: Gap Support. Five weeks on, the gap is old news. Now price is testing the gap-up low itself, and buyers are defending it. That's its own trade, with its own trigger and stop. The News Gapper pullback is different. It comes in the first days after the gap and stays above the gap-day low. Keep the two apart so you use the right stop.
questions.lesson_line: A test of the gap-up low weeks later is Gap Support.

wrong.A News Gapper pullback buy: Our pullback comes within days and stays above the gap-day low. This came weeks later, at the low.
wrong.A News Failure, the gap broke: A News Failure is a red close on the gap day. This one's a test weeks later.
wrong.A PEG, it's an earnings stock: A PEG is the report's reaction day. This is five weeks on.

questions.simple: Gap Support. Weeks later it's testing the gap-up low itself, a different trade from the first pullback.

reasons: fixed before

questions.q: What makes it an Episodic Pivot and not a plain gapper?
questions.story: A stock nobody follows has gone nowhere for six months. A contract headline gaps it 18% on 9x volume, its first gap in a year.
choices: Neglect, its first gap in months
The 18% size of the gap that day
The contract headline behind it
The 9x volume on the gap day
questions.answer: Neglect, its first gap in months
questions.why: Neglect. Nobody followed it, and it went nowhere for six months. Then a real surprise hits, and the whole market has to re-price it at once. That's the EP. The size of the gap, the 9x volume and the headline all fit a normal gapper too. What's different is that nobody was paying attention before.
questions.lesson_line: An EP is the first gap in months on a stock nobody watched.

wrong.The 18% size of the gap that day: A normal gapper can gap that far too. Size doesn't make it an EP.
wrong.The contract headline behind it: A News Gapper has named news too. The EP tell is the neglect before it.
wrong.The 9x volume on the gap day: Big volume shows up on normal gappers too. Look at what came before.

questions.simple: Neglect. A stock nobody watched gets re-priced all at once by a surprise, and that makes it an EP.

reasons: the lookalike tell comes from one criteria card
whether an EP is a version of the News Gapper is held under D-002

questions.q: Which stock earns the A+ cue for how it moved before the gap?
questions.story: Two 11% gaps on record volume. One is on a stock flat for three months. The other is on a stock up 25% in three months.
choices: Only the first; it was quiet before
Both; both have record volume
Only the second; it has momentum now
Neither; an 11% gap is too small
questions.answer: Only the first; it was quiet before
questions.why: Only the first. Quiet before the gap, not up more than about 15% in 3 months, is an A+ cue. The second ran 25% in 3 months, so it lacks it. Both gaps are 11% on record volume.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet before the gap is an A+ cue.

wrong.Neither; an 11% gap is too small: A gap of 10% or more is an A+ gap, so 11% is not small.
wrong.Both; both have record volume: Record volume is the same for both. The quiet-before-the-gap cue is not.
wrong.Only the second; it has momentum now: A run into the gap is not an A+ cue. Quiet before the gap is.

questions.simple: Only the flat stock gets the quiet-before-the-gap cue. The stock up 25% in three months does not.

deeper.example: Same gap, same volume, different months before it. Quiet before the gap is an A+ cue: not up more than about 15% in 3 months. The stock up 25% misses that cue. Up 30% or more already is a B- cue.

reasons: the 15% and 30% lines are proposed card numbers, held under D-033
all cited facts come from one criteria card

questions.q: Which close do you like better?
questions.story: Two stocks gap the same size on the same volume, and both hold the gap. One closes right at its high. The other closes mid-range, still green.
choices: The close at the high
Both the same, both held
Mid-range, more room to run
Neither, wait for tomorrow
questions.why: The one at the high. It means buyers held it all the way to the bell, and nobody was dumping into the gap. A mid-range close tells you sellers got a piece of the afternoon. Both held, so both still count. But I want the strongest close I can find. That's the cleaner setup.
questions.lesson_line: A close at the high beats a mid-range close. Buyers held it to the bell.

wrong.Both the same, both held: Both held, sure. But the high close shows buyers in charge all day.
wrong.Mid-range, more room to run: A mid-range close means sellers took a piece. That's weaker, not more room.
wrong.Neither, wait for tomorrow: The gap day's close already tells you who won the day.

questions.simple: The close at the high. Buyers held it to the bell, while a mid-range close lets sellers in.

reasons: no grade cue is tested; the close idea is the card's, with the NFLX 2018 near-miss

deeper.example: NFLX in 2018 gapped 9.2% on 3.3x volume and closed at 35% of its range. It held the gap, but sellers owned the afternoon.

questions.q: Which one do you want?
questions.story: Two stocks gap 12% on 4x volume. One gaps on a government contract that changes its business. The other gaps on an analyst upgrade.
choices: The contract, the upgrade is weak
Either, the gap and volume match
The upgrade, analysts move stocks
Same thing, a gap is a gap
questions.answer: The contract, the upgrade is weak
questions.why: The contract. It changes what the company earns, and that's real news big buyers can keep acting on. An upgrade is one person's opinion. Nothing about the business changed. The gaps and the volume match here, so the news is the only difference. And the news is what keeps buyers coming after day one.
questions.lesson_line: News that changes the business beats an opinion.

wrong.Either, the gap and volume match: They match, so the news decides it. An upgrade is weak news.
wrong.The upgrade, analysts move stocks: They move it for a day. Upgrades rarely follow through.
wrong.Same thing, a gap is a gap: Same gap, different fuel. The contract has staying power.

questions.simple: The contract. It changes the business, while an upgrade is one opinion that rarely follows through.

reasons: tied to held decisions D-032 and D-033
fixed before

deeper.counter: Bonde says analyst upgrades and media mentions have a low probability of follow-through.

questions.q: Account 40,000, risking 0.5%. How many shares?
questions.why: 104 shares. Start with the risk: 0.5% of 40,000 is $200. Then the stop distance: 105.11 minus 103.20 is 1.91 a share. 200 over 1.91 is 104.71, so round down to 104. Round down, never up. The stop picked the size, so if it hits, you lose about $200 and no more. Then check it against your position cap and take the smaller.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.
questions.simple: 104 shares. The stop sets the size, so a stop-out costs you only the 0.5% you planned.

reasons: a computed key
rests on the owner's rulebook (A5 sizing)
fixed before

choices: 382 shares
10 shares
209 shares
104 shares

wrong.10 shares: Decimal slip. You used a tenth of the risk.
wrong.209 shares: That's double the risk you set out to take.
wrong.382 shares: You multiplied by the stop distance. Divide by it.

questions.story: August 2019. You're buying the pullback reclaim after its report gap. Fill 105.11, stop 103.20.

questions.q: Take the reclaim?
questions.story: A news gap on Monday, a clean pullback, and the reclaim triggers on Thursday. The company reports Friday after the close.
choices: No, the report's too close
Yes, the reclaim is perfect
No, day 4 is too early
Yes, and hold it through the report
questions.why: No. The report is Friday after the close, so Thursday is inside the 3 days before it. Here's why we wait. A report can gap the stock overnight, and a gap jumps right over your stop. You'd be buying a fresh position with no cushion into a coin flip. We only hold through a report when the trade's already up 5R. Let the report come out, then look again.
questions.lesson_line: Report in the next 3 days means no new buy.

wrong.Yes, and hold it through the report: You hold through a report only when you're up 5R. A brand-new buy isn't.
wrong.Yes, the reclaim is perfect: A perfect chart doesn't move the report date. No new buys in those 3 days.
wrong.No, day 4 is too early: Day 4 is fine for a reclaim. The report is the problem.

questions.simple: No. A report can gap the stock past your stop, so we don't buy in the 3 days before one.

reasons: the 3-day report window is the owner's rulebook (B22)

questions.q: What now?
questions.story: Seven sessions after the gap, the stock closes under the gap-day low. You have not bought yet.
choices: Off; no Buy 2
Keep waiting for a deeper pullback
Buy at the close; it is cheap
On; only a gap fill ends it
questions.why: Off. A close under the gap-day low in the first ten sessions invalidates the setup. There is nothing to buy.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the gap-day low ends it.

wrong.Keep waiting for a deeper pullback: The gap-day low gave way on a close. Waiting does not undo that.
wrong.Buy at the close; it is cheap: Buying cheaper is not the test; the line has to hold.
wrong.On; only a gap fill ends it: A close under the gap-day low also ends it.

questions.q: Where does your stop go?
questions.story: March 2016, the day before the reclaim. A friend quotes Morales and Kacher and says give it room: put the stop 2% under the pullback low.
choices: Just under the pullback low
2% under the pullback low
Under the low of the gap day
At the prior day's close
questions.why: A few cents under the pullback low. That's where the chart says you're wrong. Morales and Kacher allow a little undercut of the gap-up low in some cases. I don't do that. The stop is the exit, so it goes right under a real low. An extra 2% of room means fewer shares for the same risk, and a bigger loss when it's wrong. ULTA's stop was about 2.2% away. That's fine as it is.
questions.lesson_line: A few cents under the low. The stop is the exit.

wrong.2% under the pullback low: That's giving it room past a real low. Our stop goes a few cents under it, and the extra room just costs you shares.
wrong.At the prior day's close: That's not a low at all. Put the stop under the pullback low.
wrong.Under the low of the gap day: The gap-day low is the line a close has to hold. Your stop sits closer, under the pullback low.

questions.simple: Just under the pullback low. Extra room means fewer shares for the same risk, and the stop is the exit.

reasons: teaches the owner's no-porosity stop over a published web view (Morales and Kacher)
the stop rule is the owner's rulebook default (F62)

questions.q: The market's just coming out of a correction. The recent earnings gappers tend to lag once it turns up.
questions.why: False, it's the other way. Coming out of a correction, the recent earnings gappers are often the ones that lead. They gapped up and held while the market was falling apart. That's strength you can't fake. So when the market turns, they're the first names I want on my list. Often isn't always, though. Each one still needs its own trigger.
questions.lesson_line: After a correction, look at the recent earnings gappers first.
questions.simple: False. They often lead, because they showed strength while the market was weak.

reasons: rests on the owner's published Sunday Scans line and the card that copies it

questions.q: Is this one you trade?
questions.story: A contract news gap jumped 20% and held. After a clean pullback, the reclaim level is $8. The stock trades about $6 million a day.
choices: No, too cheap and too thin
Yes, the gap day's volume was huge
No, a 20% gap is too late
Yes, an $8 stock is easy to size
questions.answer: No, too cheap and too thin
questions.why: No, and I wouldn't even have it on my list. We trade stocks at $10 or more that do at least $20 million a day. This one is $8 and does about $6 million, so it fails both. Thin stocks are easy to get into and hard to get out of. When it turns, there's nobody on the other side, and getting out at your stop can cost you. We also never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume.
questions.lesson_line: Ten dollars and twenty million a day, or it's not on the list.

wrong.Yes, the gap day's volume was huge: One big day doesn't change what it trades on a normal day, or the $8 price.
wrong.No, a 20% gap is too late: Right answer, wrong reason. The gap size is fine. The price and the dollar volume fail.
wrong.Yes, an $8 stock is easy to size: Cheap isn't the test. It fails the $10 line and the $20 million line.

questions.simple: No. It's under $10 and thinly traded, so getting out of a real position would be hard.

deeper.counter: One big volume day does not help. The price rule fails on its own: at $8 the stock is under the $10 line. Its usual $6 million a day also misses the $20 million line.

reasons: tied to held decision D-030 (liquidity)
rests on the owner's rulebook (B23)
fixed before

questions.q: How far is your stop, in percent?
questions.why: 2.9%. Take the fill minus the stop, 33.55 minus 32.59. Divide that by the 33.55 fill, not by the stop, and you get 2.9%. That's inside the 1 to 3% I like best. We'll take up to 5%, but tighter is better. The closer the stop, the more shares the same risk buys you. TWLO went on to reach 24.1R from here.
questions.lesson_line: Stop distance is the fill minus the stop, over the fill.
questions.simple: It's 2.9%. That's inside the range we like best, so the same risk buys you more shares.

reasons: a computed key
rests on the owner's rulebook (A13, the 3% habit)

wrong.97.1%: You divided the stop by the fill and skipped the subtraction.
wrong.28.6%: Decimal slip. That's ten times too big.
wrong.96.0%: You turned the dollar gap into a percent without dividing by the fill.

questions.story: February 2018. You bought the day-8 reclaim after its report gap. Fill 33.55, stop 32.59.

questions.q: Hold it through the report?
questions.story: You're holding a news gapper that's up 4R. The next report is tomorrow after the close.
choices: No, sell before it, under 5R
Sell, a report needs 10R to hold
Yes, the last report was a winner
Yes, the stop covers a gap
questions.why: Sell it before the report. We hold through earnings only with 5R in hand, and you're at 4R. Here's the reason. A report can gap the stock overnight, right through your stop. A bad gap can take back a lot of what you made. A 5R cushion is what lets you take that hit and still walk away with a win. At 4R it isn't there, so take the gain and look again after.
questions.lesson_line: Under 5R going into a report, sell first.

wrong.Sell, a report needs 10R to hold: Selling's right, but the line is 5R, not 10R.
wrong.Yes, the last report was a winner: The last report tells you nothing about this one.
wrong.Yes, the stop covers a gap: A stop can't catch an overnight gap. The stock can open way under it.

questions.simple: Sell first. A report can gap through your stop, and 4R is short of the 5R cushion we want.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B22 report rule)
fixed before

questions.q: So what was that loss?
questions.story: March 2024. A 15.3% gap on 15.8x volume closed at 79% of its range. You bought the day-8 reclaim at 162.59 with the stop at 158.43. It went straight to the stop.
choices: A planned loss, the stop did its job
A bad gap, never a real gapper
Proof the setup doesn't work
A rule break, stop too tight
questions.answer: A planned loss, the stop did its job
questions.why: A planned loss, and that's fine. You knew what it would cost before you bought it, and that's exactly what it cost. The gap was a great one, 15.3% on 15.8x volume. But a big gap doesn't protect the pullback buy. And look at this pullback. It gave back the whole run after the gap day, a lot looser than the quiet ones I like. Only about three in ten of these reach 3R, so plenty go straight to the stop. Take it, journal it, and move to the next one. A loss at your stop is the system working.
questions.lesson_line: A loss at your stop is the system working.

wrong.A bad gap, never a real gapper: The gap was big, on huge volume, and closed at 79% of its range. It was real.
wrong.Proof the setup doesn't work: Most buys never reach 3R. One stop-out doesn't retire a setup.
wrong.A rule break, stop too tight: The stop sat a few cents under the pullback low, right where it belongs. Getting hit isn't a rule break.

questions.simple: A planned loss. The stop set the cost before you bought, and a strong gap doesn't protect the pullback buy.

deeper.example: A 15.3% gap on 15.8x volume, closing at 79% of its range. The day-8 reclaim was bought at 162.59 and went straight to the stop at 158.43. Compare TWLO: also bought on day 8, it ran to 24.1R. The stop is what makes both outcomes acceptable.

reasons: one example from our own scan, single source, not yet owner reviewed
keyed on the stop rule, not on when the reclaim came

questions.q: Where does the pullback buy fail most often?
choices: Early reclaim after a wide day-one bar
A reclaim after a quiet 4-day pullback
A reclaim on a clean inside day
A reclaim that holds the upper half
questions.answer: Early reclaim after a wide day-one bar
questions.why: An early reclaim after a very wide day-one bar. Three of the four losing reclaims came on day 4, the earliest after a two-session pullback.
questions.lesson_line: Beware the early reclaim after a very wide first day.

wrong.A reclaim after a quiet 4-day pullback: A quiet pullback that holds the low is the good version.
wrong.A reclaim on a clean inside day: An inside day that holds the gap-day low is a good pullback.
wrong.A reclaim that holds the upper half: Holding the upper half of the gap day is an A+ cue.

questions.q: What do you do now?
questions.story: This stock gapped 11.1% on 18.2x volume, already up 23.8% over 65 sessions. You bought the day-4 reclaim at 357.70. Ten trading days in, counting the buy day, it's still under 1R.
choices: Sell it, free up the money
Hold, the stop hasn't hit
Add, it's coiling
Hold until the 20 EMA breaks
questions.answer: Sell it, free up the money
questions.why: Sell it. Ten trading days and it's still under 1R, so it's done its time. PEN made only 0.45R at best and just drifted. That money is sitting in a stock going nowhere while new setups trigger without you. The stop isn't the only way out of a trade. Time is one too.
questions.lesson_line: Under 1R after ten days, sell it and move on.

wrong.Hold, the stop hasn't hit: The time stop is built for exactly this. It drifted instead of failing, and that's still a sell.
wrong.Add, it's coiling: Not to a trade that isn't working. One buy, one price, one stop.
wrong.Hold until the 20 EMA breaks: The trail is for a winner you've already sold some of. This one never got going.

questions.simple: Sell it. Ten sessions under 1R means it's going nowhere, and that money can work in a new setup.

deeper.example: PEN gapped 11.1% on 18.2x volume and was already up 23.8% over 65 sessions. The day-4 reclaim at 357.70 reached only 0.45R. The time stop is built for a trade that goes nowhere.

reasons: the time stop is the owner's rulebook (C33)
the day count is ambiguous in the old question text, now fixed

questions.q: Is this an earnings gapper?
questions.story: April 2015. The gap day is the last bar: a 5.4% gap on 10.0x volume, closing at 90% of its range. The earnings calendar shows no report that day.
choices: No, find the headline first
Yes, the volume says so
Yes, the close says so
No, so there's no setup
questions.why: No, and that matters. The calendar shows no report, so something else moved it. Go find the headline before you do anything. About a quarter of big gaps aren't earnings, so check every time. Volume and a strong close tell you buyers showed up. They don't tell you why. And the why is how you judge how long they'll keep coming.
questions.lesson_line: Check the calendar. A quarter of big gaps aren't earnings.

wrong.Yes, the volume says so: Volume shows buyers came. It doesn't name the news. The calendar does.
wrong.Yes, the close says so: A strong close shows strength, not the cause. Check the calendar.
wrong.No, so there's no setup: A gap with no report can still be a News Gapper. It needs a headline you can name.

questions.simple: No, there was no report. Find the real headline, because the cause tells you how long buyers will stay.

deeper.trap: Calling every big gap earnings without checking is a mistake: a quarter are not. Volume and a strong close do not name a catalyst. The earnings calendar answers the first question, and the headline answers the second.

reasons: tied to held decision D-025 (who owns a no-report news gap)
fixed before

questions.q: What does that light volume do to it?
questions.story: January 2022, the day after its report. It gaps up 4.1% on 1.7x its 50-day volume and closes at its high. Our grade is how clean we judge a setup, and it sets the size.
choices: Costs it some grade, it still counts
Kills the setup, no trade
Makes it an even better buy
Only matters on non-report gaps
questions.answer: Costs it some grade, it still counts
questions.why: It costs some grade, but it still counts. AAPL held the gap and closed right at its high. That's a good day. The volume was light, 1.7x the 50-day, short of the 3x we like to see. Heavy volume raises the grade because it shows big buyers piling in. It's a plus, not a must. So this one's a lower grade and a smaller size, not a pass.
questions.lesson_line: Volume raises the grade. It isn't a must.

wrong.Kills the setup, no trade: Volume isn't a must here. It raises the grade when it's there.
wrong.Makes it an even better buy: Light volume doesn't help. Heavy volume is what raises the grade.
wrong.Only matters on non-report gaps: Volume counts the same way on every gap. It moves the grade, never the yes or no.

questions.simple: It lowers the grade but kills nothing. Heavy volume is a plus that raises the grade, not a must.

deeper.counter: Kullamägi calls volume the number one thing to focus on, and some traders treat it as a must. We say it raises the grade. AAPL's modest volume costs it grade, not its place.

reasons: volume as a grade raiser, not a must, is the owner's ruling D-006
one example from our own scan, not yet owner reviewed

questions.q: Is it a News Failure?
questions.story: October 2018. The gap day is the last bar: 9.2% on 3.3x volume. The low of the day is 35.65, above the prior close of 34.64. It closes at 35% of its range.
choices: No, the gap held, never filled
Yes, any fade is a failure
No, a 35% close is strong
Yes, it closed in the lower half
questions.answer: No, the gap held, never filled
questions.why: No. Weak, but not a failure. The low was 35.65 and yesterday's close was 34.64, so it never filled the gap. And it closed green. A News Failure closes red under the prior close, or fills the gap, and that means sellers took it all back. This one faded to 35% of its range, so sellers got the afternoon. A lower-half close like that grades a B- at best.
questions.lesson_line: A fade that holds the gap is weak, not a failure.

wrong.Yes, any fade is a failure: A fade is weak, not failed. A failure closes red under the prior close.
wrong.No, a 35% close is strong: Right answer, wrong reason. A close at 35% of the range is weak.
wrong.Yes, it closed in the lower half: A weak close isn't the failure. A red close or a filled gap is.

questions.simple: No. The gap held and it closed above yesterday's close, so it's a weak day, not a failure.

deeper.trap: A weak close is not a close under the prior close. Here the low of 35.65 stayed above the prior close of 34.64, so the gap held. That is a faded day, not a News Failure.

reasons: fixed before

questions.q: How does it grade?
questions.story: URI, 2024. A gap on earnings on 4.0x volume, close at 89% of its range, on a stock up 42% over the prior 65 sessions.
choices: Late in a run; a B- at best
A+; 4.0x volume and a high close
Fine; the close is near the high
A+; strength begets strength
questions.answer: Late in a run; a B- at best
questions.why: Late in a run, a B- at best. The stock was up 42% in the prior 65 sessions, past the line of about 30%. A late gap carries the climax risk.
questions.lesson_line: A gap on a stock already up 42% is late.

wrong.A+; 4.0x volume and a high close: Volume and the close are good; the run into the gap is the problem.
wrong.Fine; the close is near the high: A strong day does not erase a 42% run into it.
wrong.A+; strength begets strength: A big run into the gap is the late-gap warning, not a plus.

questions.q: Write the plan: entry, stop, first trim.
questions.story: PANW, 2021. An 11.6x volume gap held its low through a 6-session pullback. On day 8 the stock trades over the prior day's high at 77.06. The stop goes at 75.92.
choices: Market 77.06; stop 75.92; third at 80.48
Limit 74.00; stop 70.00; hold
Market at close; stop 77.06; 2R
Market 77.06; no stop; third at 10R
questions.why: Market 77.06, stop 75.92, a third at 80.48. One R is the fill minus the stop; three of those above the fill is 80.48. PANW reached 14.2R.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, stop and first trim, written before the open.

wrong.Limit 74.00; stop 70.00; hold: A limit far below never fills, and a stop that wide breaks the size rule.
wrong.Market at close; stop 77.06; 2R: A stop at the entry is no stop, and the first trim is 3R.
wrong.Market 77.06; no stop; third at 10R: A real stop goes in with the broker, and the first third is at 3R.

questions.q: A pullback that dips under the gap-day midpoint is graded down.
questions.why: True. A first pullback that holds the upper half of the gap day is an A+ cue. One that dips under the gap-day midpoint is a B- cue.
questions.lesson_line: Holding the upper half is A+. Under the midpoint is a B-.

questions.q: How's this pullback acting?
questions.story: November 2023. The report gap was a few sessions back, and the stock has been resting since. The last bar is today.
choices: Orderly, shallow, held the low
Broken, closed under the gap-day low
Failed, it filled the gap
Weak, any pause after a gap is a sell
questions.why: Orderly, and that's what you want. After the gap DECK just paused in small ranges. Five sessions, only 1.3% deep. It never came near the gap-day low, where the buyers first stepped in. A shallow pause like that tells you holders aren't selling. They're sitting tight. Then it reclaimed cleanly. Mark yesterday's high every night and be ready to buy it through.
questions.lesson_line: A shallow pause above the gap-day low means holders are sitting tight.

wrong.Broken, closed under the gap-day low: The gap-day low is way under these bars. No close came near it.
wrong.Failed, it filled the gap: It stayed far above the prior close. The gap never filled.
wrong.Weak, any pause after a gap is a sell: A pause is how a gapper rests. A shallow one is strength.

questions.simple: Orderly. It paused shallow and held well above the gap-day low, so holders weren't selling.

deeper.trap: A pause after a gap can look weak because price stops rising. What matters is where it closes against the gap-day low. Holding that low means the buyers who made the gap are still in. A close under it ends the setup.

reasons: no grade cue is tested; one real example from our own bars

questions.q: Are you buying this one?
questions.story: A stock has gapped up two days in a row, each day with a wider range. Today a news headline gaps it a third time on 4x volume.
choices: Pass, it's day three of a burst
Pass, the headline isn't a report
Buy day one, volume is strong
Buy the pullback tomorrow
questions.answer: Pass, it's day three of a burst
questions.why: Pass. You're looking at the third gap in a straight-up burst, with the ranges getting wider every day. That's late. Buying the third gap of a burst is a classic mistake. The stock's already stretched, and this is where climax tops happen. Big volume makes it look fresh. It isn't. I want my gaps early in a move, out of a quiet base.
questions.lesson_line: Third gap of a burst is late. Pass.

wrong.Buy the pullback tomorrow: A pullback buy still needs a setup that isn't late.
wrong.Pass, the headline isn't a report: Right call, wrong reason. Real news can be a catalyst. The problem is how late it is.
wrong.Buy day one, volume is strong: Volume doesn't fix a late gap.

questions.simple: Pass. The third gap of a burst is late, and late gaps carry climax risk.

deeper.trap: Strong volume makes the third gap look fresh. Ask where the stock is in its run. After two gaps and wider ranges it is far along, and a late gap carries climax risk.

reasons: fixed before

questions.q: What's that early volume telling you?
questions.story: A stock gaps on its report. By 9:50, twenty minutes after the open, it's already traded its full average daily volume. Our grade is how clean we judge a setup, and it sets the size.
choices: Big buyers, and it raises the grade
Nothing yet, twenty minutes is too soon
Nothing until the close
It's overheated, pass
questions.answer: Big buyers, and it raises the grade
questions.why: Big buyers are in, and it raises the grade. A whole day's average volume in twenty minutes doesn't come from small accounts. That's funds that need size and can't wait. I love seeing it on a gapper. It's a plus, though, not a must. A clean gap without it still counts, just at a lower grade.
questions.lesson_line: A day's volume in twenty minutes means big buyers. It raises the grade.

wrong.Nothing yet, twenty minutes is too soon: Twenty minutes is plenty. Early volume is the tell.
wrong.Nothing until the close: The early volume is the point. It shows who's buying right at the open.
wrong.It's overheated, pass: Heavy volume doesn't make a gap overheated. It backs the buy.

questions.simple: Big buyers are in. A full day's average volume in twenty minutes raises the grade.

deeper.trap: The early-volume reading is about speed. A big day that built slowly shows less than one that traded the average volume in the first minutes.
deeper.example: Kullamägi wants massive volume near the open, ideally the average daily volume in the first 15 to 20 minutes or even quicker.

reasons: the cue is Kullamagi's own words, used as a sign and not as a pass or fail line

questions.q: Do you take the fourth one?
questions.story: You've been stopped out of the same stock three times this week on three clean reclaims. A fourth reclaim triggers on Friday.
choices: No, three tries this week is the max
Yes, a new trigger is a new trade
Yes, at half size to cut risk
No, one stop-out bars it all week
questions.answer: No, three tries this week is the max
questions.why: No. Three tries on one stock in a week is the max, and six in a month. You've used this week's. Think about what it's telling you. Three clean setups, three stops. Whatever's going on in that name, it isn't working for you right now. A fourth try is just another loss lined up. Let the week reset and come back with fresh eyes.
questions.lesson_line: Three tries a week on one stock. Then let it go.

wrong.Yes, a new trigger is a new trade: Sure, it's a new trade. The cap on tries still applies.
wrong.Yes, at half size to cut risk: Size doesn't reset the count. The cap is on tries.
wrong.No, one stop-out bars it all week: Right answer, wrong reason. After a stop-out you can buy a new trigger, up to three a week.

questions.simple: No. You've used three tries this week, and a stock that keeps stopping you out isn't working right now.

deeper.trap: A new trigger makes it a new trade with its own stop, and that is why the fourth reclaim feels allowed. It does not reset the count of tries on that stock: at most 3 in a week and 6 in a month.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (E56 and B21)
fixed before

questions.q: Your stop math and position cap both say 666 shares of a $600 stock. It averages 40,000 shares a day. How many do you buy?
questions.why: 400 shares. We never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume. 1% of 40,000 is 400. So 400 it is, even though the stop math allows more. The reason is getting out. Own a big slice of what trades in a day and you can't sell without pushing the price down on yourself. Take the smaller number, every time.
questions.lesson_line: Own the smaller of the stop math and 1% of average volume.
questions.simple: 400 shares. We never own more than 1% of average daily volume, so we can always get out.

deeper.trap: The risk formula and the position cap would allow 666 shares. The volume cap is 1% of the stock's average daily volume, so 400 is the most. Without it you would own more than 1% of what the stock trades in a day.

reasons: a computed key
rests on the owner's rulebook (D42 and A5)

choices: 666 shares
67 shares
400 shares
4,000 shares

wrong.67 shares: You divided the volume by the price. The cap is in shares, not dollars.
wrong.666 shares: That's the stop math with the volume cap left out.
wrong.4,000 shares: That's ten percent of the volume. The cap is one percent.

questions.q: If it trades over this last bar's high tomorrow, is it a buy?
choices: Yes, the gap-day low held
Buy the close, skip the trigger
Pass, the gap-day low gave way
Pass, the gap already filled
questions.why: Yes, take it. The gap was about as good as they come. Then the pullback was four quiet days, only 2.8% deep, and every close held the gap-day low. The last bar is an inside day, tight right under the trigger. Two things I see. It's a tad extended from the 50-day, and that line is still pointing down. That's a gap out of a correction, and price is back over a rising 200-day. Neither one stops me. When price trades over yesterday's high, buy it at market. Stop a few cents under the pullback low. ULTA's was about 2.2% away.
questions.lesson_line: Held gap-day low, clean reclaim. That's the buy.

wrong.Pass, the gap-day low gave way: No close in the pullback got under the gap-day low.
wrong.Pass, the gap already filled: A 2.8% dip against a 14.2% gap never got near the prior close.
wrong.Buy the close, skip the trigger: We buy the trigger, never the close. A market order as it clears yesterday's high.

questions.simple: Yes. The pullback held the gap-day low and tightened into an inside day, so you buy it through yesterday's high.

deeper.example: March 2016: report on 2016-03-10, gap day 2016-03-11, up 14.2% on 4.8x volume, close at 94% of its range. Day 6: a buy over 190.69 with the stop at 186.55, 2.2% away. It reached 12.1R at best. One example is not a promise, but it shows what a held gap-day low and a clean reclaim can do.

reasons: one example from our own scan, single source, not yet owner reviewed

questions.story: March 2016, the day before the reclaim. A 14.2% report gap on 4.8x volume closed at 94% of its range. Then a 4-day pullback, 2.8% deep.

questions.q: January 2024. The last bar is the earnings gap day, with three months of chart before it. Buy it or pass?
choices: Pass, it was already up too much
Take it, the gap day closed strong
Take it, the volume was heavy
Pass, the volume was too thin
questions.answer: Pass, it was already up too much
questions.why: Pass. URI was already up 42% over the 65 sessions before this gap. That's late in the move. The gap day itself looked great, 5.5% on 4.0x volume, closing at 89% of its range. That's what makes it tempting. But a gap after a big run is where the climax risk lives. I want my gaps early, out of a quiet base, not after everyone's already in.
questions.lesson_line: Check the run into the gap first. A big run means pass.

wrong.Take it, the gap day closed strong: A strong close doesn't erase a 42% run into the gap.
wrong.Take it, the volume was heavy: Heavy volume doesn't make a late gap early.
wrong.Pass, the volume was too thin: Right call, wrong reason. 4.0x is strong. The run-up is the problem.

questions.simple: Pass. It had already run 42% in 65 sessions, and a gap that late carries climax risk.

deeper.trap: A strong day can hide a weak setting. The gap day closed at 89% of its range on 4.0x volume, so it looked good. But the stock had already run 42% in 65 sessions. Check the run-up first, then the gap day.

reasons: one example from our own scan, single source, not yet owner reviewed

questions.q: How clean is this one, and what's your size?
questions.story: A beat and a raise on speeding-up growth. A 12% gap on the highest volume in a year, the low above the prior day's high, a close near the high. It's out of a 4-month quiet range above a rising 200-day. The market filter reads Green. Our grade, A+ down to B-, is how clean we judge a setup.
choices: A+, so you size up
Weak, a quiet range has no momentum
Good, start small and add later
Weak, it didn't close at the high
questions.why: That's an A+, so you size up. Look at how everything lines up. A beat and a raise, a 12% true gap, the biggest volume in a year, a close near the high. And it's coming out of a quiet base above a rising 200-day, in a Green market. Nothing's fighting anything else. We don't grade off a checklist, it's a judgment. But when it all agrees like this, I want to be bigger. The stop still sets your loss.
questions.lesson_line: When the news, gap, volume, close and base all agree, size up.

wrong.Weak, a quiet range has no momentum: A quiet base is exactly where you want a gap to start from. It's early.
wrong.Good, start small and add later: We buy the full size at one price. An A+ gets its bigger size at the trigger.
wrong.Weak, it didn't close at the high: Near the high is a strong close. It doesn't have to be the exact tick.

questions.simple: A+, so you size up. The news, the gap, the volume, the close and the base all agree.

deeper.trap: We do not tick a checklist. The grade is a judgment, and it is highest when the story, the gap, the volume, the close and the base all point the same way.

reasons: a grade is discretionary (E50); the question states no checklist

questions.q: Day-one buys and pullback buys share the same trims, trail, breakeven and time stop.
questions.why: True. Both share one exit plan. The first sell is a judgment, then the stop goes to breakeven. The rest trails the 9 or 20 EMA. Under 1R after 10 sessions, either one is sold.
questions.lesson_line: The exit plan is the same for both ways in.

questions.q: What has to happen before you buy it again?
questions.story: May 2019. A 15.0% gap on 11.4x volume. You bought the day-4 reclaim at 51.76 with the stop at 50.50. It failed the next session and stopped you out.
choices: A new trigger, as a new trade
Nothing, buy it back now
Wait a full month first
Buy back half size to be safe
questions.answer: A new trigger, as a new trade
questions.why: It has to trigger again. Buying it right back because the gap was strong adds nothing new. That's the same idea that just failed. A new trigger is new information. It's a new trade, with its own stop and its own size. Until then it's just a name on the watchlist. SEDG gave the whole gap back within weeks, so waiting saved you there.
questions.lesson_line: After a stop-out, wait for a new trigger.

wrong.Nothing, buy it back now: The gap being strong isn't a trigger. Wait for the setup to fire again.
wrong.Wait a full month first: There's no month-long ban. The cap is three tries a week and six a month.
wrong.Buy back half size to be safe: Half size doesn't replace the trigger. You need a new one first.

questions.simple: A new trigger. A strong gap isn't new evidence, and a new trigger is a new trade with its own stop.

deeper.trap: A big gap on big volume can make a stop-out feel like a mistake. The day-4 reclaim at 51.76 failed the next session and the stop at 50.50 took us out. Whatever the gap looked like, the next buy needs its own new trigger.

reasons: one example from our own scan, single source, not yet owner reviewed

questions.q: So what keeps this setup paying?
questions.story: In our scan of news gappers, roughly three in ten reached 3R before the stop. The rest didn't.
choices: Small losses, selling into pushes
A wide stop that rarely gets hit
Adding when volume picks up
Skipping the pullback buys
questions.why: Small losses, and selling into strength. In the scan, 29.5% reached 3R and 19.5% reached 5R before the stop. So most of these never get far, and that's normal. The stop keeps each loss small. Then the few that work have to pay for all the rest. That only happens if you let them run and sell into the 3, 5 or 7 day pushes. Cut the losers fast and give the winners room.
questions.lesson_line: Most buys never reach 3R. Small losses and selling into pushes keep it paying.

wrong.A wide stop that rarely gets hit: A wide stop just makes the losses bigger. Ours sits a few cents under the pullback low.
wrong.Adding when volume picks up: Adds aren't the plan. One buy, one price, one stop, and an add to a winner is rare.
wrong.Skipping the pullback buys: The pullback buy is the plan, not the problem.

questions.simple: Small losses and selling into strength. Only about three in ten reach 3R, so the winners pay for the rest.

deeper.counter: Three in ten reaching 3R sounds poor. In the scan 29.5% reached 3R and 19.5% reached 5R before the stop, so most buys never reach 3R. The stop sets the size of each loss, and the first sell is a judgment, often into a 3, 5 or 7 day push.

reasons: a scan result that can change
fixed before

questions.q: In the 60 sessions before a gap, the high was 58.00 and the low was 46.00. How far is the high above the low, in percent?
questions.why: 26.1%. The high minus the low is 58.00 minus 46.00. Divide that by the low, 46.00, and show it as a percent. That is under the 35% line, so the 60 sessions were a quiet range, the setting our card prefers. A base of 4 weeks or more is the card's other preferred setting.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet means the 60-session high is within 35% of the low.
questions.simple: The high is about 26.1% above the low, under the 35% line, so the range was quiet.

reasons: a computed key
fixed before

wrong.126.1%: Divided high by low and forgot to subtract one.
wrong.260.9%: Decimal slip: ten times too big.
wrong.79.3%: Took the low as a share of the high and skipped the gap.

questions.q: How was it set up before this gap?
choices: A long quiet range, no big run
A steep run, up a lot in weeks
A long, steady slide
A sharp crash just before
questions.answer: A long quiet range, no big run
questions.why: A long, quiet range. PANW went sideways for about six months, then gapped 13.7% on 11.6x volume right out of it. That's what I want to see. A gap out of a quiet base is early in its move, so there's room to run. A gap after a big run is late, and that's where climax tops come from. Always look left before you buy the gap.
questions.lesson_line: A gap out of a quiet range is early in its move.

wrong.A steep run, up a lot in weeks: Look again. The six months before were a sideways range, not a run.
wrong.A sharp crash just before: No crash. It ranged for months.

questions.story: August 2021. The report gap day is the last bar. Look at the six months before it.
questions.simple: A long quiet range. A gap out of a quiet base is early, while one after a big run is late.

reasons: the 35% quiet-range number is no longer tested (rule 22); one real example from our own bars
